syllabusTopics: Hydrogen: chemistry of atomic and nascent hydrogen; isotopes of hydrogen and their uses
Application of hydrogen as fuel; heavy water and its applications
Allotropes of oxygen: definition of allotropy and examples; oxygen — types of oxides (acidic, basic, neutral, amphoteric, peroxide and mixed oxides)
Applications of hydrogen peroxide; medical and industrial application of oxygen
Ozone: occurrence, preparation of ozone from oxygen, structure of ozone, test for ozone, uses of ozone
Ozone layer depletion: causes, effects and control measures

Chemical properties of nitric acid: HNO3 as an acid and oxidizing agent (action with zinc, magnesium, iron, copper, sulphur, carbon, SO2 and H2S); ring test for nitrate ion
Halogens: general characteristics of halogens; comparative study on preparation, chemical properties (with water, alkali, ammonia, oxidizing character, bleaching action) and uses of Cl2, Br2 and I2
Test for Cl2, Br2 and I2

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Hydrogen peroxide's career is one decomposition equation played a dozen ways: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. The **antiseptic fizz** in a 3 % wound wash is catalase running it; the **gentle bleach** of hair, silk, wool and pulp is its selective oxidation sparing protein fibres where chlorine bleaches would chlorinate and weaken them; the **detergent's** perborate and the **rocket's** 85 % HTP live off the same oxygen release;…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ - Volume strength: x V ⇒ M = x/11.2; % w/v = 3.4 × M ≈ 0.304 × V - 10 V ⇒ M = 0.893 M, ~30.4 g/L ≈ 3 % w/v - 2Fe²⁺ + H₂O₂ + 2H⁺ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2H₂O - 2KMnO₄ + 3H₂SO₄ + 5H₂O₂ → 2MnSO₄ + K₂SO₄ + 8H₂O + 5O₂

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Bleach That Bleaches Itself Hydrogen peroxide wears two hats: **oxidant** (bleaching hair, textiles, pulp; antiseptic) and **reductant** (decolourising KMnO₄, reducing Ag₂O). Oxygen's industrial roles run from steelmaking to welding. This topic collects the uses, the concentration language (volume strength), and the storage precautions.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Applications of hydrogen peroxide - **Medical (3 % solution):** antiseptic for wounds — oxidises bacterial tissue; releases oxygen on contact with the enzyme catalase (bubbling action cleans debris).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: M = volume strength / 11.2 (10 V -> 0.893 M; 3% w/v). Dual nature: oxidant with Fe2+, reductant with KMnO4. Storage trio: cold, dark, wax-lined. Steel = LD converter; flame ladder: oxy-hydrogen 2800, oxy-acetylene 3200.

rows.text: **NEB-style (2m numerical): Calculate the molarity of a 10-volume hydrogen peroxide solution.** — "10-volume" means that 1 volume of the solution liberates 10 volumes of oxygen gas at STP on complete decomposition: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂. rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One decomposition equation runs the whole topic: 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ — it is the antiseptic's bubble, the bleach's mechanism, the rocket's thrust and the reason storage must be cold, dark and wax-lined.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: H2O2 uses: 3% antiseptic (catalase bubbling), bleaching hair/silk/wool/pulp (gentle oxidation, no chlorine residue), detergent perborates/percarbonates, water and effluent treatment (cyanide, phenol), HTP ~85% rocket propellant.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Every tonne of basic-oxygen steel takes about 50–60 m³ of oxygen — the gas that keeps us alive is mostly consumed keeping bridges and cars standing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why are metal containers forbidden for H2O2 storage?  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Volume strength is not molarity:** 10-volume ≠ 10 M — the conversion is M = V/11.2 (10 V → 0.893 M); using /5.6 double-counts the stoichiometry.  ·  **Antiseptic H₂O₂ is 3 %, not 30 %:** 30 % is laboratory/rocket strength and burns skin — quote the right concentration per use.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Decomposition is not "evaporation":** H₂O₂ losing strength on storage is chemical decomposition (2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂) catalysed by light and metals — hence wax-lined, dark, cold storage.  ·  ## 7.
